state.notice_text:
NOTICE
To, Ms. Anjali Mehta
You were employed with our firm and left without serving notice. As per Section 13 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 and Section 7 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you are liable to pay us Rs. 30,000 as compensation for leaving without notice. Pay within 7 days of receipt of this notice, otherwise we will take strict legal action.
HR Department, Nexa Solutions Pvt Ltd, 5 November 2026

CPA2019:s107.heading: Repeal and savings
CPA2019:s107.text:
107. (1) The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 is hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken or purported to
have been done or taken under the Act hereby repealed shall, in so far as it is not inconsistent
with the provisions of this Act, be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding
provisions of this Act.
(3) The mention of particular matters in sub-section (2) shall not be held to prejudice
or affect the general application of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 with regard to
the effect of repeal.
10 of 1897.
————
DR. G. NARAYANA RAJU,
Secretary to the Govt. of India.

COW2019:s69.heading: Repeal and savings
COW2019:s69.text:
69. Repeal and savings .—(1) The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (4 of 1936), the Minimum Wages 
Act, 1948 (11 of 1948), the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 (21 of 1965) and the Equal Remuneration Act, 
1976 (25 of 1976) are hereby repealed. 
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the enactments so repealed 
including any notification, nomination, appointment, order or direction made there under or any amount 
of wages provided in any provision of such enactments for any purpose shall be deemed to have been 
done or taken or provided for such purpose under the corresponding provisions of this Code and shall be 
in force to the extent they are not contrary to the provisions of this Code till they are repealed under t he 
corresponding provisions of this Code or by the notification to that effect by the Central Government. 
(3) Without prejudice to the provisions of sub -section (2), the provisions of section 6 of the General 
Clauses Act, 1897 (10 of 1897) shall apply to the repeal of such enactments.
COW2019:s69.full_text:
69. Repeal and savings .—(1) The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (4 of 1936), the Minimum Wages 
Act, 1948 (11 of 1948), the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 (21 of 1965) and the Equal Remuneration Act, 
1976 (25 of 1976) are hereby repealed. 
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken under the enactments so repealed 
including any notification, nomination, appointment, order or direction made there under or any amount 
of wages provided in any provision of such enactments for any purpose shall be deemed to have been 
done or taken or provided for such purpose under the corresponding provisions of this Code and shall be 
in force to the extent they are not contrary to the provisions of this Code till they are repealed under t he 
corresponding provisions of this Code or by the notification to that effect by the Central Government. 
(3) Without prejudice to the provisions of sub -section (2), the provisions of section 6 of the General 
Clauses Act, 1897 (10 of 1897) shall apply to the repeal of such enactments.

explanation.plain_summary: Ms. Anjali Mehta has received a notice from her former employer demanding Rs. 30,000 as compensation for leaving without notice, with a 7‑day deadline for payment. The notice cites sections of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 and the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, but both of those statutes have been repealed and replaced by newer laws.

claims.text: Section 13 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 no longer exists because the entire Act was repealed by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (see CPA2019:s107).
claims.quote: The Consumer Protection Act, 1986 is hereby repealed.

claims.text: Do not panic; note the date you actually received the notice (not the notice’s own date).
Gather any employment contract, resignation letter, salary slips, and any prior correspondence with the HR department.
Consider contacting free legal aid services (e.g., Legal Services Authorities) to review the notice and advise on any possible remedies.
Because the cited statutes are repealed, the legal basis the employer relies on is doubtful; a lawyer can help assess whether any other law or contract term applies.

cannot_assess: Whether the employer’s demand of Rs. 30,000 is contractually justified, as the employment agreement and any company policies are not provided.
lawyer_needed_when: You are unsure about the contractual obligations regarding notice period and compensation.
The employer threatens legal action and you need to understand the possible claims they might bring under current law.

kind.is: A letter from an employer (warning, termination, recovery, or reply to your claim).
is_not: It is not a decision by a labour authority or court.

options.name: Ignore it
options.risk: Silence can be read as not disputing their claims, and you lose track of any deadline they set. Not recommended without advice.

options.name: Send a short factual reply
options.risk: Anything you write can be used later. Stick to facts, deny what is wrong, admit nothing you are unsure of.

options.name: Negotiate / ask for documents
options.risk: Asking for the documents they rely on costs little and buys time, but note their deadline.

options.name: Pay what they ask
options.risk: Ends the dispute fast but may mean paying something not owed. Get it in writing as full and final settlement.

options.name: Get free legal help first (DLSA / NALSA 15100)
options.risk: Takes a little time; do it well before their deadline.

result.reply_warning: A reply to a legal notice can create admissions. Keep it short and factual, do not apologise for things you did not do, and have an advocate or the DLSA check it if the amount matters to you.
threats: we will take strict legal action.
gather: The notice and its envelope / courier slip (proves when it reached you)
Any agreement, bill, invoice or messages the notice refers to
Proof of any payments you already made
A note of the date you received it and how (post, courier, WhatsApp, email)
